---
title: SQL playground
description: Run SQL against the latest Cancer Basemap release in your browser with DuckDB-Wasm. Nothing to install.
---

Edit the query and press **Run**. It runs in your browser with
[DuckDB-Wasm](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview), against
`latest/` attached as `basemap` (and selected with `USE basemap`, so
`measure.observation` works as well as `basemap.measure.observation`). The
first run downloads DuckDB itself, a few MB. Until the first release is
published the attach fails and the box shows the error.

Queries that filter and use `LIMIT` are fast, because DuckDB fetches only the
parts of each Parquet file it needs. Full scans of the big tables
(`measure.observation` has tens of millions of rows) are slow and can run out
of browser memory. For those, use DuckDB on your own machine
([Versions and citation](guides/versions-and-citation.qmd)).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
duckdb = import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.33.1-dev57.0/+esm")

conn = {
  const bundle = await duckdb.selectBundle(duckdb.getJsDelivrBundles());
  const workerUrl = URL.createObjectURL(
    new Blob([`importScripts("${bundle.mainWorker}");`], { type: "text/javascript" })
  );
  const db = new duckdb.AsyncDuckDB(new duckdb.VoidLogger(), new Worker(workerUrl));
  await db.instantiate(bundle.mainModule, bundle.pthreadWorker);
  // Read byte ranges only. By default DuckDB-Wasm downloads each whole
  // Parquet file before querying it. All three flags are needed: leaving
  // forceFullHTTPReads unset breaks every open.
  await db.open({
    filesystem: { reliableHeadRequests: true, allowFullHTTPReads: false, forceFullHTTPReads: false }
  });
  const c = await db.connect();
  await c.query("ATTACH 'https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/cancerbasemap.duckdb' AS basemap (READ_ONLY)");
  await c.query("USE basemap");
  return c;
}

viewof sql = Inputs.textarea({
  label: "SQL",
  value: `SELECT geo_id, period_start, value, value_status
FROM measure.observation
WHERE source = 'PLACES' AND source_release = '2025'
  AND measure_id = 'PLACES:MAMMOUSE:age_adjusted'
  AND geo_id LIKE 'county:08%'
ORDER BY geo_id
LIMIT 100;`,
  rows: 8,
  width: "100%",
  monospace: true,
  submit: "Run"
})

result = {
  const t0 = performance.now();
  try {
    const table = await conn.query(sql);
    // int64 columns arrive as BigInt, which the table view can't format.
    const rows = table.toArray().map((r) =>
      Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(r.toJSON()).map(([k, v]) =>
        [k, typeof v === "bigint" ? Number(v) : v]))
    );
    return { rows, seconds: (performance.now() - t0) / 1000 };
  } catch (e) {
    return { error: e.message };
  }
}

result.error
  ? html`<div class="alert alert-danger" role="alert"><pre class="mb-0">${result.error}</pre></div>`
  : html`<p class="small" id="playground-status">${result.rows.length} rows in ${result.seconds.toFixed(1)} s ·
      <a href="${window.basemapShellUrl(sql)}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open in DuckDB Shell ↗</a></p>`

Inputs.table(result.rows ?? [], { rows: 15 })
```

## Queries to try

Copy one into the box, or open it in the DuckDB Shell.

```sql
-- Every table in the database
SELECT schema_name, view_name
FROM duckdb_views()
WHERE database_name = 'basemap' AND NOT internal
ORDER BY 1, 2;
```

```sql
-- A cell the source did not report never reads as a number
SELECT value_status, count(*) AS n, count(value) AS with_value
FROM measure.observation
GROUP BY value_status
ORDER BY n DESC;
```

```sql
-- The provenance of this release
SELECT release, published_at, git_sha
FROM read_json('https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json');
```
